title: Cubital Tunnel Syndrome (Ulnar Nerve at the Elbow)
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Tingling and numbness in the little finger and half of the ring finger, and the back of the hand on that side. Medial elbow ache. In more advanced cases: clumsiness, weak pinch, wasting of the first dorsal interosseous (between thumb and index finger), clawing of the ring and little fingers.
working: Cubital Tunnel Syndrome (Ulnar Nerve at the Elbow)

differentials.name: Guyon canal (ulnar nerve at the wrist)
C8 radiculopathy
differentials.key: Neck signs, medial forearm involved, thumb flexor weakness

qa: Why does phone use worsen symptoms? Sustained elbow flexion compresses and stretches the ulnar nerve.
What does a positive Froment sign show? Weak adductor pollicis from ulnar motor involvement.
Dorsal ulnar hand sensation is normal, little finger numb. Where is the lesion? Likely at the wrist (Guyon canal).
When should you refer for surgery? Progressive weakness or wasting, or no improvement after adequate conservative care.
Why sliders rather than tensioners? Less provocation of a sensitive nerve.

fields.Position and action: Full elbow flexion with wrist extension, held up to 60 s
As above, with finger pressure over the nerve behind the epicondyle
Tap over the nerve in the groove
fields.Meaning: Supports nerve irritation; common in healthy people too

fields.Position and action: Patient holds paper between thumb and side of index finger while you pull
fields.Positive: Thumb tip flexes (flexor pollicis longus substitutes for weak adductor pollicis)
fields.Meaning: Motor involvement of the ulnar nerve

redFlags.Finding: Wasting with fasciculations, no sensory loss

manualNotes: Education and activity change (main treatment): avoid prolonged elbow flexion and leaning on the elbow; use a headset for phone calls.
Night splint or towel wrap: keep the elbow at about 30 to 45 degrees of flexion while sleeping [Ref – to verify]. Nerve sliders: gentle ulnar nerve gliding (Vol 13 Ch 5), no strong tensioning.
Strengthening of hand intrinsics if weak.
